subject: Authorization request: APAC warm-standby traffic drain & EU transition window
messages:
From: Alicia Mendez <amendez@finxpay.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@financecloud.co>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: APAC warm-standby + EU transition — residency constraints and authorization

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're preparing a scheduled switchover test: primary EU (Frankfurt) -> primary APAC (Singapore) failover for regional maintenance next month. Before we sign off on the runbook we need explicit authorization details for two items:

1) APAC warm-standby traffic drain: when we move inbound traffic to APAC, we require an approved drain window that ensures any cached KV data that is PII-indexed is either invalidated or remains encrypted under our customer-managed keys. We also need to confirm the step that prevents EU data from being copied to any transient object storage outside DE/SG/AU.

2) EU transition window: the return cutover (APAC -> EU) must be scheduled with a maximum RTO of 20 minutes and an observable audit trail showing the route change, BGP propagation, and request affinity. We need evidence the plan will not cause cross-border egress (exceptions must be documented).

Attached is our internal checklist and the current SLA constraints. Can you send the authorization request template (who at Redwood signs) and a short technical checklist covering routes, peering, KMS keys, and log retention we can attach to our change request?

We'd like to lock a tentative date week of Dec 6, prefer nightly drain 02:00–03:00 local SG time. Please loop in engineering and compliance as needed.

Best,
Alicia
Chief Product Officer, FinX Pay
attachments: finx-internal-sw-turnover.docx (referenced)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Mendez <amendez@finxpay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 12:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: APAC warm-standby + EU transition — residency constraints and authorization

Alicia,

Thanks — appreciate the clear ask. We've drafted an authorization package and a technical validation checklist to map to the items you called out. Key points up front:

- Redwood will not copy persistent EU customer blobs outside of the approved jurisdictions (DE, SG, AU) during the switchover; transient caches (KV prefix caches) are handled per configuration and can be invalidated before cutover.
- KMS: we will use customer-managed KMS where configured; for keys we don't manage we will perform crypto-wrap operations so plaintext never crosses regions.
- Auditability: Routing events, API traces, and token flows will be exported to your audit log bundle (S3 link) and signed with our runbook signature.

Action: attaching our warm-standby authorization checklist (xlsx) and a short adoption window proposal. Please review and confirm approval for the window: Dec 7, 02:00–03:00 SGT (Dec 6 evening UTC). We request 48 hours heads-up to complete pre-cutover validation.

Next steps from our side once you approve:
- Karthik to run a pre-cutover BGP/peering dry-run and provide expected propagation times.
- Mina to produce a compliance affirmation stating no cross-border egress will occur and what logs we will hand off.
- Jordan to coordinate stakeholder comms and post-cutover rollback authority.

If that sounds good I'll schedule a pre-cutover tech call Tuesday.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
attachments: warm-standby-authorization-checklist.xlsx (stated), kms-key-map.csv (stated)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Mendez <amendez@finxpay.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 07:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: APAC warm-standby + EU transition — routing/peering notes

Marissa / team,

Quick technical notes for the checklist (I'll produce a short runbook fragment by Tue):

- Peering/BGP: we'll pre-announce the APAC prefixes from the warm-standby pool with a lower local-pref during the dry-run to estimate convergence. Expect 3–8 minutes for regional propagation within the provider fabric and up to 12 minutes to reach some downstream caches depending on upstream ISP policies.
- NAT / Egress gating: configure DNAT rules on the APAC edge to preserve source IP where FinX requires affinity. We will also apply strict egress ACLs so any EU-origin traffic is dropped; this is a fail-closed setting during the drain.
- KV cache handling: implement pre-cutover prefix invalidation for session-affine caches and a post-cutover soft-warm-up to avoid cache stamping. For any persistent state, we'll rely on cross-region read-only replicas under explicit control; write path will be disabled until keys and tenancy are validated.
- KMS mapping: we'll bind customer KMS keys in DE for EU data. For APAC we will use the customer's SG/AU keys if provided; otherwise use envelope encryption under your key policy.

Attachments: I'll include a small tracer snapshot (apac-egress-trace.png) from our last sim to demonstrate propagation.

Cc'ing Alicia so FinX sees the expected propagation window.

-karthik
Senior Network Eng, Redwood Inference
attachments: apac-egress-trace.png
From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Mendez <amendez@finxpay.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 06:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: APAC warm-standby + EU transition — compliance checklist and audit artifacts

Team / Alicia,

Compliance notes for the package:

- Audit artifacts: We'll provide a signed bundle containing (a) routing-change events with timestamps, (b) token-level access logs for the 2-hour window bracketing the switchover, and (c) a KMS key rotation ledger if any re-wrapping occurs. These will be time-synced to FinX's audit timezone and shipped to your approved S3 destination.
- Data residency proof: a short report demonstrating object store placement (S3/GS buckets) and access origin for the test window. This will show there were no object copies outside DE/SG/AU.
- Retention & rollback: We will retain the audit bundle for 90 days by default (extendable), and we'll snapshot the router state to enable rollback within your RTO.

Two items I need from FinX for the final affirmation: (1) list of customer-managed KMS key ARNs for SG/DE/AU, (2) confirmation that the post-cutover telemetry export endpoint is the S3 path in your change request.

If those are provided I will sign the compliance affirmation and upload the artifacts post-test.

-mina
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
attachments: kms-key-map.csv

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@financecloud.co>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: APAC warm-standby + EU transition — authorization and approval

Marissa,

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and detailed notes. FinX approves the proposed window Dec 7, 02:00–03:00 SGT (we'll file the change request today).

Per Mina: we'll send you the KMS ARNs for DE and SG by EOD. The S3 export endpoint for telemetry is: s3://finxpay-audit-redwood/2027-12-07-warm-standby.

One ask: can Redwood provide a short readout after the test (15–20 minute replay) that includes the signed audit bundle and the BGP propagation snapshot? If so, we'll schedule a post-test review on Dec 8.

If everything above is in order I'll mark the runbook approved on our side.

Appreciate the team aligning on tight notice.

Best,
Alicia
Chief Product Officer, FinX Pay
